name: Generalized Essential Telangiectasia

criteria.description: Presence of widespread telangiectasias involving multiple body regions without underlying systemic disease
No evidence of systemic connective tissue disease or hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia
Onset of telangiectasias typically in early to mid-adulthood
No family history of hereditary telangiectasia syndromes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of widespread telangiectasias in multiple body regions without systemic disease or family history of hereditary telangiectasia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and exclusionary; genetic testing may be performed to rule out hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia.

pathognomonic.notes: Widely distributed dilated superficial blood vessels visible on skin
Macules remain red upon pressure due to vascular dilation
searchTerms: persistent red spots that don't fade
red flat skin marks that stay

common.symptomName: Telangiectasias on upper and lower extremities
searchTerms: small red blood vessels on arms and legs
tiny red skin spots on extremities
red blood vessels on face and chest
spider veins on trunk and face
small red skin spots on upper body

common.symptomName: Mild skin dryness or irritation over affected areas
Intermittent mild bleeding from telangiectatic lesions
searchTerms: occasional mild bleeding from red spots
light bleeding from small blood vessels

occasional.notes: Occasional involvement of oral or nasal mucosa
searchTerms: red blood vessels inside mouth or nose
tiny red spots on mouth lining

occasional.symptomName: Mild pruritus localized to telangiectatic areas
searchTerms: mild itching on red skin areas
episodes of sudden skin warmth and redness
red blood vessels on eye surface

rare.symptomName: Epistaxis related to nasal mucosal telangiectasias
searchTerms: bleeding from nose due to vessel abnormalities
bleeding from small gut blood vessels
occult blood loss in digestive tract

rare.symptomName: Anemia secondary to chronic blood loss
searchTerms: low red blood cells from ongoing blood loss

laboratory: Normal blood counts typically; anemia if chronic bleeding present
imaging: No vascular malformations on imaging studies
genetic: No mutations in ENG, ACVRL1, or SMAD4 genes (genes associated with hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia)
other: Clinical exclusion of systemic diseases such as scleroderma or hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia

distinguishingFeatures: Family history of telangiectasia and arteriovenous malformations
Genetic mutations in ENG, ACVRL1, or SMAD4
Presence of skin atrophy, pigmentation changes, and telangiectasia

redFlags: Recurrent severe epistaxis or gastrointestinal bleeding
Signs of systemic connective tissue disease
references: Bolognia JL, Schaffer JV, Cerroni L. Dermatology. 4th ed. Elsevier; 2018.
James WD, Berger TG, Elston DM. Andrews' Diseases of the Skin: Clinical Dermatology. 13th ed. Elsevier; 2019.
